Lessons.Title: Use a Protractor to Measure Angles
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will understand \(1^\circ\) as a measurement of a turn through \(\frac{1}{360}\) of a circle and to use a protractor to measure angles.
Before this lesson, you have compared and measured angles using informal tools (analog clocks) and reference angles, all of which were multiples of \(5^\circ\) or multiples of \(10^\circ\) . In this lesson, you transition to measuring angles in units of \(1^\circ\) . You then make sense of one-degree angles in terms of a fraction of a \(360^\circ\) turn and are introduced to the protractor as a tool of measurement.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: True or False: There's Something about 45 (10 minutes); Activity 1: How Large is a $1^\circ$ Angle? (15 minutes); Activity 2: Use a Protractor (20 minutes); Cool-down: Measure the Angles (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Align a protractor's center with the vertex, its baseline with one ray, and read the scale beginning at zero on that ray.

Edulytics authored guidance: Recognize that 1° is one out of 360 equal parts of a full turn. Place the protractor center on the angle vertex and align zero with one ray. Read where the second ray crosses the same scale, and reject the other scale if it contradicts the angle's size.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Draw and measure an angle of 65° with a protractor.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
